question: The fertiliser action plan has set the goal of mobilising a total of EUR 540 million. Achieving this will involve increasing the agricultural reserve with an extra EUR 300 million from the EU budget for 2026, which Member States could then top up nationally by up to 200 %. However, previous opt-in schemes have shown that Member States rarely commit their share of the funds.

A case in point is the wine package: here the Commission has enabled up to 100 % co-financing to combat flavescence dorée, and yet vineyards in Croatia, for example, are being ravaged as the government has yet to take any action to avail of the possibility. In light of the above: Does the Commission intend to oblige Member States to make use of the national financing option?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (7.8.2026) As part of the short-term initiatives envisaged in the Fertiliser Action Plan1 adopted on 19 May 2026, the Commission has prepared an exceptional support package2 for European farmers facing high fertiliser and other input costs funded through the agricultural reserve.

The support package will offer immediate liquidity relief for farmers ahead of the next production cycle and help sustain agricultural production. The Implementing Regulation includes a provision allowing Member States to grant additional support up to a maximum of 200% of their corresponding national allocations, which are set out in the Annex to the act. This is a possibility for Member States.
The Commission does not intend to oblige Member States to make use of the national financing option.
